references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's servant who gives his back to those who strike: "I offered my back to those who beat me" – a prophetic parallel to the whipping Jesus predicted in [ref:Jes 50:6|Isaiah 50:6].
Isaiah's prophecy about the suffering servant who was wounded and crushed for our transgressions points forward to Jesus' suffering and death that he predicts in [ref:Jes 53:5|Isaiah 53:5].
The prophecy that the Lord's servant would be taken away from the land of the living and given a grave corresponds to Jesus' prediction about his death in [ref:Jes 53:8-9|Isaiah 53:8-9].
The prophecy "on the third day he will raise us up" from Hosea is an Old Testament background for Jesus' prediction of resurrection on the third day in [ref:Hos 6:2|Hosea 6:2].
Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day to the disciples, parallel to Luke 18:33, in [ref:Matt 16:21|Matthew 16:21].
The second prediction of suffering in Matthew where Jesus says he will be killed and raised on the third day, corresponding to [ref:Matt 17:23|Matthew 17:23].
Matthew's parallel to Luke 18:33 where Jesus specifically mentions whipping and crucifixion, as well as resurrection on the third day, in [ref:Matt 20:19|Matthew 20:19].
Mark's parallel account of this third prediction of suffering, where Jesus predicts he will be mocked, spat upon, whipped, and killed, and raised after three days, in [ref:Mark 10:34|Mark 10:34].
Peter's Pentecost sermon confirms the fulfillment of Jesus' prediction: God raised him up and freed him from the pains of death, in [ref:Apg 2:23-24|Acts 2:23-24].

Paul confesses the early Christian creed that Christ died, was buried, and rose on the third day according to the Scriptures – the fulfillment of what Jesus predicted in [ref:1 Kor 15:4|1 Corinthians 15:4].

The angel at the empty tomb reminds the women of Jesus' own words that he must be crucified and rise on the third day – a direct reference to the prediction in Luke 18:33, in [ref:Luk 24:6-7|Luke 24:6-7].
The fulfillment of the prediction about whipping: Pilate had Jesus whipped, in [ref:Joh 19:1|John 19:1].
